title: Airgap OCI proxy CICD promotion and rollback (draft)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This working draft captures an operational playbook for delivering images and releases into air-gapped / VPC/private deployments using a proxied OCI registry sync approach. Focus is on reproducible artifact promotion, signature-based attestation, Terraform module hooks for infra, and clear rollback/upgrade mechanics for GitOps (Argo) + Helm-managed clusters.

Goals:
- Provide a minimal blast radius promotion flow that doesn’t require manual artifact copying inside customer airgaps.
- Ensure images and manifests are cryptographically verifiable (cosign + SBOM) before install.
- Standardize Terraform module outputs/inputs needed to wire the registry proxy and Argo/GitOps sync jobs.
- Define a clear canary / staged rollout and deterministic rollback path.

Assumptions / constraints:
- Customers may be fully air-gapped or have an outbound-proxy/OCI-mirror device that can pull from a staging registry on our side.
- Use cosign for image signatures; Rekor transparency is optional in airgap mode (we rely on detached signatures distributed with artifacts).
- ArgoCD is used as the GitOps engine inside customer clusters and Helm is used for chart templating.
- Terraform is used to provision on-prem connectivity objects (registry-proxy deployment, S3-like blob store, KMS keys).

High-level architecture (textual):
1) CI (hosted): build -> generate SBOM (syft) -> sign image (cosign) -> push to hosted staging OCI registry -> publish release metadata (artifact bundle includes image digest, signature blob, sbom).
2) Promotion service: upon promotion trigger, create a signed promotion manifest (promotion token) and enqueue artifact to proxy sync queue.
3) Customer-side OCI proxy / mirror agent: periodically polls secure promotion queue (mutual TLS) and pulls artifacts into local registry; validates signatures using provided public key bundle; stores artifacts locally and serves them to Kubernetes.
4) GitOps: promotion step commits an update to the customer Argo repo (image digests / Helm values) or flips a channel tag; Argo sync picks up and applies.

Checklist (pre-promotion):
- [ ] Build artifacts reproducibly (pin base images, record build env).
- [ ] SBOM generated and attached (syft or similar).
- [ ] Image signed with cosign; signature exported alongside SBOM and manifest.
- [ ] Promotion manifest produced with artifact digests and signature validation metadata.
- [ ] Terraform run created/validated (registry-proxy credentials, KMS keys accessible, sync cron scheduled).

Promotion flow (detailed):
1) CI produces artifact bundle and calls /internal/promotion-service with release-tag and list of bundles.
2) Promotion service verifies signatures against known good signing keys (dev keyring + rotation policy).
3) Promotion service writes a promotion record to the proxy queue (signed by promotion-service key) with TTL.
4) Customer proxy polls signed queue endpoint (mTLS). The proxy validates promotion record signature and requested digests.
5) Proxy pulls OCI manifest + layers directly from hosted registry. On pull complete, proxy verifies cosign signature and checks SBOM sanity.
6) If verification passes, proxy writes artifact into local registry and updates its internal index to mark availability.
7) Promotion service optionally opens a PR to customer GitOps repo updating values/image.digest or flips the channel ref.
8) Argo detects change and begins sync constrained by rollout config (see rollout config below).

Signature and SBOM handling notes:
- Use cosign with KMS-backed keys in hosted mode. For customer airgap, we ship a public key bundle + signed promotion manifests.
- For full airgap customers who cannot access Rekor, include detached signatures and signed SBOMs in the artifact bundle.
- SBOM verification in the proxy is mandatory for high-assurance customers. Keep a small set of SBOM rules (e.g., no critical CVEs above X, required package provenance fields).

Terraform module notes (interface draft):
- Module name: redwood/airgap/proxy
- Inputs (string): proxy_image, proxy_cron_schedule, allowed_origins, s3_endpoint, s3_bucket, registry_hostname_internal, tls_cert_secret_name, kms_key_id
- Inputs (list): sync_whitelist (list of repositories or name patterns)
- Outputs (string): proxy_endpoint, credentials_secret_name, public_key_bundle_secret, sync_status_webhook
- Lifecycle considerations: the proxy should be deployed as a long-running daemonset/Deployment with persistent disk for local registry cache. Provide lifecycle rules to drain before upgrades.
- Recommended resource sizing: start with 4vCPU/16GiB and scale to 16vCPU/64GiB for a full model artifact catalog.
- Example usage snippet (pseudocode):
  module \"proxy\" {
    source = \"github.com/redwood/modules//airgap/proxy\"
    proxy_image = \"registry.redwood.ai/proxy:stable-202502\"
    s3_endpoint = var.s3_endpoint
    s3_bucket = var.bucket
    registry_hostname_internal = var.registry_host
    tls_cert_secret_name = \"proxy-tls\"
    kms_key_id = var.kms_key
  }

Argo/GitOps patterns and repo layout (recommendation):
- repo-root/
  - clusters/
    - customer-a/
      - apps/ (helm values per app)
      - env/ (global env values)
  - artifacts/ (signed promotion manifests, read-only)
  - promos/ (automated PRs live here; PRs must contain: image digest, promotion token)

Rollout configuration (Argo + Helm hooks):
- Canary strategy: start with 3% of replicas or a single replica per node pool depending on cluster topology.
- Health checks: application-level readiness + SLO-based query (95th latency) hook. If health fails for 10 minutes, rollback.
- Helm chart must expose an annotation for image.digest and image.signature so Argo can use exact digests rather than tags.
- Pre-sync hook: run a verification Job that validates the signature on the pulled image in-cluster (cosign verify using public-key secret). If verification fails, abort sync.
- Post-sync hook: smoke test Job that runs a small e2e check; if the smoke test fails, trigger automated rollback.

Automated rollback strategy (clear steps):
1) Argo detects failing health check or post-sync smoke test fails -> automatically revert to last known-good commit (repo revert).
2) Proxy retains previous artifact versions for a configurable retention window (7–30 days recommended).
3) If revert commits previous image digests, Argo will sync back to prior release.
4) If image needs to be removed from local registry (security), run proxy garbage-collect flow and update RBAC for forensic review.

Edge cases and failure modes:
- Partial sync (some layers failed): proxy should mark artifact as corrupt and alert operators; do not update image index.
- Signature key rotation: maintain overlap window where verifier accepts both old and new keys; scripted rotation through promotion-service endpoint.
- Large model layers causing OOM: proxy must support chunked downloads and restart/resume.
- Drift between declared digest and deployed image: have a periodic attestation job that reconciles deployed digest vs repo digest and alerts if mismatched.

Helm upgrade considerations and hooks:
- Use Helm 3 with --atomic disabled for complex operator upgrades; instead rely on argo sync with pre/post hooks for custom retries.
- Provide a chart lifecycle hook to quiesce processing workloads before a database schema migration.
- When upgrading operator CRDs: use a two-step approach where new controller is deployed next to old controller, CR migration jobs run, then old controller removed. Document these steps in upgrade notes.

Operational playbook (runbook style):
- PREPROMOTE (operator): verify CI bundle, run local signature validation against public key bundle, ensure Terraform proxy module is stable (no pending drift).
- PROMOTE: trigger promotion-service -> observe proxy queue -> watch customer proxy logs for pull+verify success.
- APPLY: watch Argo PR sync -> ensure pre-sync verification Job succeeds.
- MONITOR: check latency/cost telemetry and SLOs for 30m after rollout.
- ROLLBACK: if SLOs breach or smoke test fails, revert Git commit and escalate to oncall.

TODOs / open questions:
- Decide whether promotion service should push a signed commit directly to customer GitOps repo vs opening a PR.
- Define hard limits and throttles for proxy concurrent pulls to avoid saturating customer egress.
- Flesh out key rotation playbook with concrete scripts that run in-staff-only mode and a separate limited flow for enterprise customers.
- Investigate using imgpkg/kon/pkg for reproducible bundle transport vs raw OCI layers.

References / helpful commands (dev notes):
- cosign sign --key kms://gcp/locations/us/keyRings/ring/cryptoKeys/key image@sha256:<digest>
- cosign verify --key publickey.pem image@sha256:<digest>
- syft packages image@sha256:<digest> -o json > sbom.json
- example Argo pre-sync hook job: kubectl apply -f hooks/pre-verify-job.yaml

Notes to self:
- Keep this doc intentionally pragmatic—customers hate heavy lift. Automated promotion + signed artifacts is the right path; avoid mandating Rekor for customers that cannot reach the public internet.
- Share with solutions engineering before finalizing Terraform interface.

Change log:
- 2025-02-14: initial draft (Aisha)
- 2025-02-21: added Terraform module sketch and example usage (Miguel)
- 2025-03-02: added more explicit rollback flow and SBOM handling (Ravi)

End of draft.
